newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee looking weak, could break ranges.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee looking weak, could break ranges.

text.p: NOV Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures are likely to extend their bear trend as a series of weak performances threatens to wipe out most of this year's gains, technical analysts said on Friday.
The London market was called to open unchanged to a touch higher than Thursday's close.

The second-month November contract has bounced off $1,500 support for two consecutive sessions, but analysts said the market's technical outlook was still bearish in the longer term even though support might hold for now.
"I think we might see another day of consolidation with $1,500 holding the market, maybe getting up as far as $1,550," said Darren Gurner, analyst at Sucden.
"But I definitely think we're going to see an eventual break of $1,472...the market is in a bear trend and it has been since the day we crashed down," he said.
London's trading pattern had been one of lower daily troughs coupled with lower highs, suggesting a definite bearish scenario, Gurner said.

A small breakaway gap created in January between $1,355 and $1,408 should also act as a downside hurdle, but once broken would signify that the market would have retraced most of the gains amassed since January.

In fundamental news, Brazilian producers said a sharp fall in coffee received by cooperatives in past months proved that this season's harvest was markedly lower than last year, and not higher as suggested by the USDA.
This week the growers' National Coffee Council (CNC) said that 1.16 million 60-kg bags of coffee had been received by cooperatives during July, bringing the total since May to 1.96 million bags.
This was down 30 percent from the 2.80 million bags delivered in the same period in 1996, with the 1996/97 crop now widely thought to have been between 25 million and 28 million bags.
